subject: Data sovereignty pricing: rollforward discount vs. annual surcharge

Subject: Data sovereignty pricing: rollforward discount vs. annual surcharge

Hi Steve / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — glad the pilot went well. Attached is a concise proposal that outlines two paths for the compliance/security add-ons you asked about (audit logs retention, KMS/HSM seats, and US data residency):

1) Tiered rollforward discounts (recommended for pilots that convert to scale)
   - 6/12/24 month discount bands tied to committed usage.
   - One-time implementation credit (amortized across first 12 months) to offset migration costs.
2) Annual surcharge model (preferred by some procurement teams)
   - A fixed annual fee for residency + HSM seats with no upfront credits; lower discount on usage.

Key tradeoffs called out in the doc:
- Upfront credit lowers OPEX impact in year 1 but requires a longer committed term to amortize.
- Surcharge simplifies invoicing but increases unit cost on tokens/embeds.

I attached: Redwood_Compliance_Pack_Workback_v1.pdf (workback and cost table) and a draft SOW placeholder.

As next steps, can you confirm which route procurement prefers and any internal constraints (PO cadence, fiscal quarter cutoffs)? If you prefer, Ben and I can sketch a blended option (partial credit + reduced surcharge) and run it through finance.

Best,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Data sovereignty pricing: rollforward discount vs. annual surcharge

Jordan — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few follow-ups from procurement and security: 

1) Procurement asks whether the implementation credit can be delivered as a monthly invoice credit (vs. a single netted credit) — that helps our internal bookkeeping.
2) Security flagged that HSM seat pricing needs to include a short SLA addendum clarifying rotation/access controls (we'll share exact language).
3) On residency: we must ensure evidence (SOC2 + attestation of region-level keys) is delivered within 30 days of contract signature or procurement will push for a higher surcharge.

A few constraints:
- CuraTrust's fiscal year closes 9/30; procurement wants to lock terms before 9/1 to hit FY approvals.
- Preferred billing cadence is quarterly.

From a deal economics standpoint, we prefer a predictable annual surcharge (easier for finance), but we are open to a blended approach if the first-year implementation credits can be shown as distributed monthly and capped.

Can you (or Ben) put up a quick table showing cashflow impact for each option (year 1 vs year 2) and a recommended legal clause for the HSM access SLA? That will speed procurement sign-off.

Regards,

Steve — joining with a short economic / implementation note. Quoting your ask: "Can you put up a quick table showing cashflow impact for each option (year 1 vs year 2) and a recommended legal clause for the HSM access SLA?"

Summary recommendation (high level):
- Offer a blended model: 50% of the implementation credit delivered as a monthly invoice credit over 12 months, plus a reduced annual surcharge (30% lower than the standalone surcharge).
- Rationale: keeps procurement's predictable annual spend lower than the pure surcharge route, spreads the credit to match your quarterly books, and gives Redwood some protection via a 12-month minimum commitment on compliance features.

Attached quick table (pasted inline):
- Option A (Tiered rollforward): Year1 cashflow = Low OPEX (credit reduces invoices ~40%), Year2 = Normalized usage pricing (committed discount applies)
- Option B (Annual surcharge): Year1 cashflow = Higher fixed fee + no credits, Year2 = Lower marginal cost but higher baseline spend
- Option C (Blended, recommended): Year1 cashflow = Moderate fixed (reduced surcharge) + small monthly credit; Year2 = near Option A economics but with better cashflow smoothing

Proposed SLA language for HSM (draft, please have legal review):
"Redwood will maintain KMS/HSM key material and access controls within the agreed-upon US region. Redwood shall provide attestation of key custody controls and a SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days of contract execution. Any requested technical evidence (key rotation logs, access list) will be delivered under an NDA and via the agreed evidence delivery schedule."

Operational asks:
- Laura / Mina: can finance/legal greenlight the monthly-credit mechanism (does it create risky revenue recognition exposure)?
- Steve: what PO cadence do you need for us to present a final signed quote (quarterly billing + monthly credit amortization will require a PO referencing the SOW).

If helpful, Jordan and I can run a quick 15–20 minute screen share to walk the CFO's team through the cashflow table.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

- Blended offer (final): 12-month minimum for compliance bundle; implementation credit = $75k delivered as a monthly invoice credit of $6,250; reduced annual residency surcharge set at $120k/year (vs $170k standalone). Committed usage band gets standard rollforward discounts if you hit the tiers in the Workback.
- Evidence delivery: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II and a resident-key attestation within 30 days of signature; additional rotation logs available within NDA window.
- Invoicing: quarterly billing; credit line applied as invoice line item each month.

2) Upload DocuSign contract (I included a link in related_links).

Thanks — look forward to closing this and starting the residency onboarding.
